history.sg_progress: The Administration will continue to send monthly statements to the agencies on their outstanding receivables and strengthen its efforts to encourage agencies and other United Nations entities to pay their dues, including their share of contributions to the health insurance funds, on a timely basis. The Administration will also take measures to expedite the reconciliation process of outstanding health insurance receivables to avoid long-outstanding balances and ensure that payments are received from the agencies. With respect to the outstanding receivable balances from the participating entities for the United Nations Staff Mutual Insurance Society, the Administration has implemented appropriate measures, reaffirming its commitment to preventing long- outstanding balances. Consequently, there are no long-standing receivables and the open receivables balance, as at 30 June 2024, consisted exclusively of recently billed amounts owed by participating agencies for services rendered in 2024.

history.administration_response: The recommendation was implemented. The Administration has conducted a systematic review of outstanding and unmatched items and identified the underlying causes. The Administration has reconciled and cleared the open balances of $24 million from the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Administration has conducted a systematic review of outstanding items, and reconciled and cleared the open balances of $24 million from the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
